title: U.S. House · Indiana's 8th District
area: Southwestern Indiana, including Evansville, Vincennes, and Jasper.

context.text: Incumbent Mark Messmer ran unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Mary Allen won the Democratic primary with 66.7% of the vote over three challengers.

summary.text: Mark Messmer is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 8th Congressional District, a mechanical engineer and former Indiana state senator first elected to Congress in 2024. He was endorsed by President Donald Trump and Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Purdue University (1985).
Professional experience includes co-owner of Messmer Mechanical and project engineer roles with John Brown Engineering and Dow Chemical.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry), the Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Received the presidential endorsement of Donald Trump in 2026.

priorities.text: Describes himself as pro-life and credits his Indiana statehouse work with the state's abortion restrictions since Roe v. Wade was overturned.
priorities.quote: Thanks to my work in the Statehouse, Indiana now has the most protective Pro-Life legislation in the nation since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

priorities.text: Supports securing the southern border and ending birthright citizenship for people in the country illegally.
priorities.quote: We need to secure the southern border and deport the illegal immigrants that Joe Biden has allowed to flood into our country. We need to end birthright citizenship for people that are here illegally.

priorities.text: Supports a cryptocurrency regulatory overhaul that promotes blockchain innovation and opposes central bank digital currencies.

positions.summary: Opposes abortion access and points to his role in passing restrictive Indiana abortion legislation.
positions.quote: As a Right to Life endorsed candidate as well as the ONLY candidate endorsed by Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America, I will continue to defend the unborn and work to expand adoption and other abortion alternatives.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border, deporting people in the country illegally, and ending birthright citizenship for undocumented immigrants; as an Indiana state senator voted for bills allowing law enforcement to detain undocumented immigrants who committed felonies, banning sanctuary universities and cities, and requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.
positions.quote: I have voted to allow law enforcement to detain illegal aliens that have committed a felony until immigration officials can take them into custody (SEA590). I voted to ban sanctuary universities (SEA243). I co-authored a ban on sanctuary cities (SEA181), and voted to require proof of citizenship to register to vote (HEA1264).

positions.summary: Supports Israel's sovereignty and right to defend itself, and opposes boycott, divestment, and sanctions (BDS) movements against Israel.
positions.quote: I steadfastly support Israel's sovereignty and its unwavering fight for survival amidst threats... I oppose these movements unequivocally, standing in solidarity with Israel.

record.text: As an Indiana state senator, voted for SEA 590 allowing law enforcement to detain undocumented immigrants who committed felonies until immigration officials take custody.
As an Indiana state senator, voted for SEA 243 banning sanctuary universities and co-authored SEA 181 banning sanctuary cities.
As an Indiana state senator, voted for HEA 1264 requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.
Introduced a bill on Ready Reserve Force modernization in the U.S. House.
Announced passage of the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act in the House of Representatives.

candidates.name: Mary Allen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 66.7% of the vote.

summary.text: Mary Allen is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 8th Congressional District, an Evansville small business owner, Army Reserve veteran, and at-large member of the Evansville City Council.

background.text: Lives in Evansville, Indiana; served in the U.S. Army Reserve.
At-large member of the Evansville City Council, where she has also served as council vice president.
Has served on the Vanderburgh County Solid Waste Board and the Evansville Metropolitan Planning Organization, and chaired the Enterprise Zone.

priorities.text: Says families are struggling with an affordability crisis: rent, groceries, and healthcare costs outpacing wages, and supports fair markets and breaking up corporate monopolies she says are squeezing workers and farmers.
priorities.quote: We are in an affordability crisis. Families earning minimum wage need over full-time hours to afford a modest apartment... Corporate monopolies have rigged the system.

priorities.text: Says healthcare should be a right, citing rising insurance premiums, drug costs, and surprise medical bills.
priorities.quote: She believes accessible and affordable healthcare is a right, not a privilege.

priorities.text: Wants Congress to listen more to constituents' concerns on education, immigration, healthcare, and affordability rather than repeating national talking points.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a right, criticizes Medicaid cuts, and warns of rural hospital closures in Indiana.
positions.quote: We've watched the Trump administration cut Medicaid by a trillion dollars while rural hospitals close their maternity wards and emergency rooms. In Indiana, five rural hospitals are at risk of closing entirely.

positions.summary: Supports real wage increases that keep pace with inflation.
positions.quote: Mary will fight for real wage increases that keep up with inflation, fair markets and breaking up monopolies, and an economy that works for working people.

summary.text: James Burke is an independent candidate for Indiana's 8th Congressional District, a Terre Haute native who says he is running a social-media-only campaign without fundraising.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Terre Haute South High School, completed a carpenter's apprenticeship, and attended Western Governors University.

priorities.text: Supports raising taxes on companies with large profits to fund universal healthcare, and says big money should not have a place in elections.
priorities.quote: I believe if the billionaires pay their fair share we can have universal health care... I believe big money has no place in our elections and both houses of congress need to get back to working with the people.

priorities.text: Supports LGBTQ+ rights, marriage equality, and describes himself as pro-choice and pro-union.

positions.summary: Supports taxing highly profitable companies to fund universal healthcare and points to high ambulance and medical costs as a policy priority.
positions.quote: The absorbent price of Healthcare, $4000 for a 5 minute ambulance ride, having to file bankruptcy or lose everything you've worked for because you got sick.

positions.summary: Supports taxing highly profitable corporations more heavily, saying large companies should either pay a living wage or be taxed.
positions.quote: there's no reason a company making 100 billion net profit should have any employee needing assistance.
